title: Total Drama: Carnival of Chaos
subtitle: A season of rigged games, broken showmances, exposed advantages, and one final challenge where Jade turned calculation into a crown.

winner.name: Jade
winner.keyStats: Jade wins with 3 challenge wins, 3 immunities, 10 votes against, and a finale victory decided on the field rather than by jury ballot.
winner.strategy: Jade plays like a quiet knife: gathering loyalty early, spending idols aggressively, cutting social threats before they harden, and letting bigger personalities take the blame until the endgame forces her into the open.
winner.legacy: Her legacy is cold, controversial, and undeniable — a winner who survives public blowups, broken alliances, and jury hostility by making the last challenge her final argument.

placements.name: Jade
placements.notes: Jade wins by weaponizing perception, loyalty, and endgame challenge power when the jury no longer has the final say.
placements.story: Jade enters the carnival already reading faces, and the season quickly bends around that skill. She builds early trust with Hannah, Benji, Ivy, and Zaid, then repeatedly chooses timing over comfort, even when it costs her friendships. Her game is never clean; it is sharp, reactive, and often personal, especially once Spencer and Anastasia become permanent obstacles. The post-merge reveals her as a kingmaker hiding in plain sight, credited for the Zaid, Marissa, and Spencer boots while absorbing betrayals from people she once protected. By the finale, the jury may be divided on her morality, but the format gives her one final arena instead of one final argument. Jade wins the Carnival Rescue because every mental obstacle is just another pattern to solve.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Chose the selfless Survival Kit at the Summit and immediately raised her tribe's comfort and trust.
Episode 6: Found the Red Team idol and quietly became the best-protected player on her tribe.
Episode 9: Played an idol for Zaid, wiping out votes and proving loyalty could be weaponized.
Episode 19: Won Night of the Killer Clown immunity by beating Isabel in a photo finish.
Episode 20: Helped drive the Marissa vote, earning jury credit as a hidden kingmaker.
Episode 22: Flipped off Spencer after his overplay, ending one of her longest rivalries.
Episode 24: Won Bumper Car Bash and secured a finale seat.
Episode 26: Won the final Carnival Rescue and the season.
placements.personality: Jade was calm, watchful and deliberately reassuring, often positioning herself as the person who steadied the group while privately admitting she sometimes made things “wobble” to see what happened. She tested people with planted information, kept track of who watched whom, and treated trust as something to measure through leaks and reactions. Her softer attachment to Benji complicated that approach, but even late in the season she still spoke in clipped commands and strategic reads rather than open emotion.

quotes.text: I don't break spirits. I just notice things.
Zaid is the only person in this camp I trust with a coconut, a vote, or a plush banana. That's a hierarchy.
A clown attacked me.

trivia: She repeatedly used fake information to test Benji, once inventing that Zaid had asked about Spencer’s puzzle numbers and later inventing that Ivy was going after him.
She described trusting Zaid with “a coconut, a vote, or a plush banana.”
She kept giving short tactical instructions, including “Keep it hidden,” “Benji watches Hannah. Ivy watches Benji. You watch Ivy,” and “Keep climbing.”

placements.name: Logan
placements.notes: Logan reaches the final as a social-physical hybrid whose bonds keep him alive even after his alliances collapse around him.
placements.story: Logan begins as the upbeat strongman who makes Blue Team feel functional even when the shelter leaks and the food disappears. His best work happens in conversations: with Marissa, Isabel, Anastasia, Richard, and later Jade, he becomes the person people use to test their plans. But the deeper the season goes, the more his deals overlap, and the more jurors see a player who can soothe a room while quietly moving a vote. He wins key immunities, saves himself at the exact right times, and survives the collapse of The Ride or Die by staying useful to everyone left. His finale loss is not a collapse; it is the pain of reaching the final line and finding out the season will be decided by one more race. Logan leaves as the runner-up who played people better than he played the final obstacle.
keyMoments: Episode 3: Helped form The Triumvirate with Natalia and Richard, then immediately showed how unstable his loyalties could be.
Episode 10: Melted down in Hell's Kitchen but remained central enough to survive the fallout.
Episode 14: Won immunity with Isabel in the treasure dive and helped redirect the vote that sent Natalia out.
Episode 17: Survived the lie-detector challenge fallout while his name became openly dangerous.
Episode 19: Warned Isabel to play her idol, saving her and damaging his own alliance credibility.
Episode 21: Won paired immunity with Jade in Wheel of Misfortune.
Episode 25: Won Say Cheese immunity and became an automatic finalist.
Episode 26: Lost the final Carnival Rescue to Jade.
placements.personality: Logan came across as earnest, loyal and easily rattled by the pressure of the game. He wanted to be the kind of person who kept a handshake deal, apologized when conditions were worse than expected, and jumped in when Marissa was stuck rather than calculating the cost. His confessionals often showed him second-guessing himself, but in camp he was blunt when honesty was required, including admitting, “I voted for you.”

quotes.text: I shook Richard's hand. I told him final two. I'm not the guy who breaks that on night one. I'll write Ted, everyone else can write whoever, it'll work out. [pause] Right?
quotes.context: in confessional after making a deal with Richard

quotes.text: Marissa disappeared into the ground! One second she was there, the next she was shoulders and anger. I didn’t think. You don’t leave your people in a mud hole.
I thought we were okay.

trivia: He compared Isabel’s final-two offer to being “invited into a really nice house and realizing there are no windows.”
He complained that he had only had one funnel cake in forty-eight hours.
He was repeatedly shown physically helping with camp or challenges, including hauling scrap wood with Natalia and catching a tilting fence with Hannah.

placements.name: Anastasia
placements.notes: Anastasia plays the season's loudest strategic game, wins three immunities, and gets cut by the jury the moment she is vulnerable.
placements.story: Anastasia arrives angry, and somehow turns that volatility into leverage. She finds an idol early, survives a massive idol play at the merge, and keeps her name in every major strategic conversation even when rivals openly call her controlling. Her bonds with Marissa and Logan give her warmth, but her feuds with Isabel, Jade, Spencer, Lynda, and Natalia give the season its heat. The deeper she goes, the more her résumé grows and the more the jury understands that she has been steering from the smoke. But that visibility becomes fatal. At final three, Logan wins immunity, the jury gets the knife, and Anastasia is removed not because she cannot win — but because too many people believe she can.
keyMoments: Episode 4: Found the Blue Team hidden immunity idol and kept it secret.
Episode 14: Played her idol and negated four votes in the biggest advantage play of the season.
Episode 18: Bought and played a Vote Steal that helped redirect Jade's vote onto Ivy.
Episode 20: Won Maze of the Fallen immunity by remembering eliminated players better than the field.
Episode 21: Won The Princess Pride duel against Prince Spencer by a hair.
Episode 24: Secretly flipped the vote onto Hannah after Hannah overplayed.
Episode 25: Received the disadvantage in Say Cheese and still nearly survived before the jury eliminated her.
Episode 25: Left with a furious accusation that exposed Jade's endgame control.
placements.personality: Anastasia was controlled, intense and openly strategic, with a habit of turning social conflict into something she could choreograph. She watched for clues, tracked who had power, and was willing to “edit” the truth if it produced the reaction she wanted. Over time she showed flashes of self-correction, admitting when her comments had not helped, but she never stopped sounding like someone who expected to manage the board.

quotes.text: Ted never said that. Ted has never said one word to me about Alessio. But Alessio's face just did the math I wanted it to do. That's not lying. That's editing.

They think that was a fight. That was choreography. I picked Richard because Richard is confused by his own shoes. Nobody watched me leave, because nobody wanted to watch me leave. [pulls out the totem] And I got a friend.
quotes.context: in confessional after getting the totem

quotes.text: The person I betray tonight is someone I’ll face tomorrow.

trivia: She spent forty-two minutes searching paths, rocks and benches because she believed Richard had grabbed an idol clue.
She once stood completely still staring at Tristan until he froze mid-laugh.
She guarded her bag at camp, and later pulled a bag away from Jade hard enough that chalk spilled over Jade’s shirt and face.

placements.name: Hannah
placements.notes: Hannah is the season's social engine, a provider and connector who repeatedly shapes votes until her own relationships become too threatening.
placements.story: Hannah starts by learning names, building fires, and making people feel like they matter. That understated work becomes power, especially in the Red Team structure where she helps steer early decisions while appearing less dangerous than Jade, Spencer, or Benji. Her midgame is defined by intense bonds — Jade, Zaid, Ivy, Benji, Logan — and those relationships become both her résumé and her exposure. At final ten, the jury credits her with the Richard boot, a sign that her influence is finally visible. But by the endgame, the same warmth that kept her safe becomes a jury-threat warning sign. Anastasia and Logan cut her at four because Hannah sitting at the end is a story nobody wants to face.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Captained Red Team's shelter build and made everyone feel useful.
Episode 2: Spearheaded The Anchor vote that sent Amelie to Rescue Island.
Episode 4: Helped target Diego, surviving a tense tied vote and tiebreaker outcome.
Episode 17: Organized the negotiated flip on Richard and received broad jury credit for the move.
Episode 20: Formed The Shield Wall with Jade as an endgame survival structure.
Episode 22: Joined the failed push against Logan while Spencer was cut instead.
Episode 24: Overplayed at tribal and became the final-four casualty.
Episode 24: Left asking whether Anastasia's bond with her had ever been real.
placements.personality: Hannah was sharp, social and observant, often noticing the emotional current of the tribe before others said it aloud. She respected Jade’s steadiness but also watched for cracks in it, and she built a quieter understanding with Ivy that did not need constant declarations. When cornered, she could be blunt and cutting, but she also noticed who needed someone and who was doing the work without asking for credit.

quotes.text: Zaid just said "the vote is obvious tonight" like the walls don't have ears. The walls have ears, dude. The walls are ME.
Ivy and I have a thing now. Not an alliance — something quieter. Like... we both know we can look at each other and know what the other's thinking. That's rare out here.
Starve.

trivia: She called Amelie “first boot” once on the first night and later defended the read in confessional.
She noticed Jade snapping at her because Jade was usually so calm.
She and Jade sometimes reacted in sync, including both speaking at the same time in episode 21.

placements.name: Spencer
placements.notes: Spencer survives eight dangerous votes as a brilliant, abrasive tactician before the room finally punishes his overplaying.
placements.story: Spencer is planning from the moment he steps off the bus, and for a long time that brain keeps him alive. He forms The Anchor with Jade, breaks it, rebuilds elsewhere, gets swapped instead of eliminated, and keeps finding cracks inside majority plans. His greatest strength is also his fatal flaw: every conversation becomes an angle, every ally becomes a calculation, and eventually everyone can feel the machinery. His feud with Jade hardens into one of the season's defining rivalries, while his battles with Anastasia and Logan add new fronts he cannot fully manage. By final five, he is still alive after nineteen votes against him, a record of both danger and resilience. Then he whispers too loudly, scrambles too visibly, and the window closes thirty minutes before he can counter it.
keyMoments: Episode 2: Formed The Anchor with Jade, briefly positioning himself as a core strategist.
Episode 4: Voted against Jade and shattered The Anchor from inside.
Episode 8: Was voted out but survived via Elimination Swap, moving to Blue Team instead of leaving.
Episode 9: Bought critical information when he spotted Zaid pocketing an idol clue or advantage clue on the carousel.
Episode 15: Survived a three-way tiebreaker that eliminated Benji instead.
Episode 18: Bought individual immunity at auction, escaping a dangerous vote.
Episode 20: Overheard Jade bragging from the Maze pit and gained ammunition he never fully used.
Episode 22: Overplayed at final five and was voted out after eight escapes.
placements.personality: Spencer was analytical, tense and deeply bothered by not having a read on everyone. He treated conversations like data, kept track of who was useful as a person versus as a vote, and hated when someone else spoke as if they controlled his choices. His confidence in his own competence was real, but so was his tendency to spiral when Jade, alliances or challenge mistakes made him feel outmaneuvered.

quotes.text: There's eighteen people here. I've clocked sixteen of them. Alessio, I have no read on. He's either the smartest guy in this game or he has a concussion. I cannot tell which and it's eating me alive.
I have thrown a coconut before. I have. In my life. Just — not today. Today I am a man who has never seen a coconut.
quotes.context: in confessional after a bad challenge

quotes.text: Zaid thinks loyalty makes him difficult to manipulate. It doesn’t. It means you have to know which relationship to press.

trivia: He found or carried a clipboard almost immediately and stood by the lumber pile without touching the lumber.
He identified Ivy as “the keystone” to his path forward.
He gave very dry one-word or near-one-word answers in camp, including “Owl,” “Yes,” “Good,” and “Obviously.”

placements.name: Isabel
placements.notes: Isabel is a villainous social tactician whose idol save buys her one more round before old grudges finally catch up.
placements.story: Isabel enters with arrogance, and somehow backs enough of it up to become indispensable. She burns relationships early, especially with Marissa, Natalia, Richard, and Anastasia, but she also builds working ties with Logan and Lynda that keep her strategically relevant. Her game thrives in whispers, intimidation, and perfectly timed mistrust. She finds a merge idol, holds it through chaos, and plays it when Logan warns her, erasing votes and sending Zaid home instead. But the idol cannot erase the way people feel about her. At six, Spencer, Hannah, and Anastasia finally land the shot, and Isabel exits realizing that being heard is not the same as being feared enough.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Clashed with Marissa immediately, setting up one of the season's earliest hero-villain dynamics.
Episode 3: Kissed Lynda in Truth or Dare Train and deepened a complicated Blue Team bond.
Episode 9: Formed The Ride or Die with Logan and Lynda as a late pre-merge safety net.
Episode 16: Found the merge hidden immunity idol.
Episode 19: Played her idol after Logan's warning, nullifying votes and surviving the Zaid boot.
Episode 20: Survived the Marissa vote by a single vote.
Episode 21: Was voted out after her feud with Anastasia became impossible to contain.
placements.personality: Isabel was commanding, resentful and comfortable being the person who took charge when everyone else was emotional or hungry. She collected slights, especially from Marissa, and converted small conversations into names, reads and leverage. She could sound cold even when she admitted a deception was unpleasant, treating enjoyment as irrelevant if the move worked.

quotes.text: Somebody has to run this. Everybody's crying about Tribal and about food and nobody's actually DOING anything. So fine. I'll do it. I'll be the mean mom. But we'll eat.
Lynda is useful. She gathers people, takes blame naturally and believes our friendship is stronger than it is. I don’t enjoy deceiving her. Fortunately, enjoyment is not required.
I’m welcome to survive.

trivia: She fixated on Marissa after Marissa criticized her in front of everyone.
She grabbed an extinguisher in episode 10.
She described the Ride or Die as working for exactly one vote.

placements.name: Marissa
placements.notes: Marissa plays a heroic, physically capable, fiercely loyal game that makes her beloved and therefore expendable at seven.
placements.story: Marissa starts as the person willing to say what others will not, staring down Isabel before the game has even settled. She becomes the weight-bearer of Blue Team: provider, emotional outlet, challenge performer, and half of multiple unbreakable bonds. Her loyalty to Logan and Anastasia gives her purpose, while her rescue of Zaid in the treasure dive gives her one of the season's defining hero moments. But loyalty also narrows her options. When the game turns on pairs, her bond with Anastasia becomes weather everyone plans around. Jade's coalition cuts her at seven, and Marissa leaves naming Jade as the real author of the vote.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Publicly confronted Isabel and established herself as the season's early hero figure.
Episode 5: Dominated A-Maze-ing Grip as Blue Team's coconut dunker.
Episode 14: Abandoned a winning path underwater to rescue Zaid from drowning.
Episode 17: Won Hung Out to Dry immunity over the shark tank.
Episode 18: Joined the live coalition that eliminated Ivy, damaging several bonds.
Episode 20: Tried to move against Spencer but was countered and voted out.
Episode 20: Exited warning everyone that Jade made the call.
placements.personality: Marissa was practical, suspicious and prone to feeling overlooked even while others came to her with problems. She built shelter plans, remembered who searched what, and reacted strongly when she thought someone had left her exposed or blamed her unfairly. Her bond with Logan was one of quiet trust rather than constant strategy talk, while her later conversations with Anastasia showed she could name flaws without pretending they did not exist.

quotes.text: What is HAPPENING with everyone today. Did I miss a memo? Is there a memo?
Logan and I don't need to talk about it. We look at each other, and we know. That's what happens when you actually trust someone.
Nobody really asks how I’m doing.

trivia: Her first camp line was a detailed lean-to plan using long boards, the shed wall and a tarp.
She repeatedly said she came into the game alone or came there alone.
She got lost in the corn and later insisted, after a pause, that this was what happened.

placements.name: Zaid
placements.notes: Zaid is the loyal soldier and fan favorite whose bonds repeatedly save others until his own betrayals leave him exposed.
placements.story: Zaid begins as the easygoing connector who can make camp laugh, then slowly becomes a central emotional force. His connections with Jade, Ivy, Hannah, and Marissa are real, messy, and strategically dangerous. He survives idol drama, showmance fallout, and multiple plans against him, often by being someone people cannot quite bring themselves to cut. But Zaid also takes credit he should not take, flips when pressure hits, and leaves scars on alliances that once protected him. By the time Ivy is gone and the Campfire Crew has fractured, his loyalty story no longer matches his voting record. Jade and Spencer finally put him down while Isabel's idol detonates the rest of the night.
keyMoments: Episode 3: Stole credit for Spencer's Amelie blindside, starting a long strategic grudge.
Episode 6: Built an unbreakable bond with Ivy that became a liability.
Episode 8: Received an idol from Jade on the walk to tribal, deepening their trust.
Episode 9: Was saved by Jade's idol play after Benji and Ivy wrote his name.
Episode 14: Nearly drowned in the treasure dive and was revived by Marissa.
Episode 18: Voted Jade after her tribal overplay, breaking Campfire Crew trust.
Episode 19: Was eliminated after Isabel's idol nullified the other path.
placements.personality: Zaid tried to be calm, loyal and fair, but his confessionals showed how much strain that role put on him. He cared about promises and people, especially Benji, yet he also admitted when he flinched or voted in a way that made him feel worse. His humor surfaced under pressure, but so did fear that nobody asked how the reliable guy was doing until after he broke.

quotes.text: I voted Benji. Alone. Because I didn't want to pull the trigger on Spencer when it looked like it was slipping. That's not a play, that's a flinch. [pause] I flinched.
Benji's loyal. Benji's a mess right now, but he's loyal. And a loyal mess is worth ten calm liars. I'll take it.

[rubs his face] I blew up. I know. I'm supposed to be the calm one, the reliable one, the "let's all get along" guy. But you know what? The calm one is tired. And the reliable one is scared. And nobody asks the "let's all get along" guy how he's doing until after he loses it.
quotes.context: in confessional after losing his temper

trivia: His first notable moment was a silent two-second stare with Natalia across the crowd.
He warned Benji to stop eating grey-centered corn dogs, only for Benji to ask if dizziness meant they were working.
He described his bond with Ivy as “building another road” rather than replacing anyone.

placements.name: Ivy
placements.notes: Ivy returns from the Edge and immediately resumes as the season's emotional backbone, only to be cut twice for being too connected.
placements.story: Ivy's game is built on care before calculation, and that makes her both loved and hunted. Early on, she becomes a social center in Red Team, forming deep ties with Jade, Zaid, Benji, Hannah, and Spencer. Her showmance-adjacent bonds become impossible to hide, and the game punishes her the first time at the pre-merge Red Team vote. She wins her way back at the Edge, proving that her social strength is matched by nerve under pressure. But the second act is harsher: she is too close to too many people, and her attempt to move on Logan leaks into a counterstrike. Anastasia's Vote Steal helps seal it, and Ivy leaves heartbroken more than angry.
keyMoments: Episode 3: Revealed her secret on Truth or Dare Train without hesitation.
Episode 6: Built an unbreakable bond with Zaid after the spin-the-bottle spark.
Episode 12: Was blindsided by Jade and Hannah despite deep personal bonds.
Episode 16: Won the Edge return gauntlet and re-entered the game.
Episode 17: Outlasted much of the cast in Hung Out to Dry before losing grip late.
Episode 18: Tried to build a Logan vote that leaked and triggered the counterattack.
Episode 18: Was eliminated after Anastasia stole Jade's vote and redirected it onto her.
placements.personality: Ivy was socially aware, flexible and anxious beneath a composed surface. She made multiple final deals, noticed when Hannah withheld information, and understood that Jade and Zaid becoming a “bonded-unit thing” was a problem to solve before it hardened. Her warmth still showed in small gestures, but her confessionals made clear that she was constantly recalculating who was safe, who was too close, and which promise might become dangerous.

quotes.text: Amelie's really nice? But she's, like, VERY nice. Like when someone at the mall says your shoes are cute and then follows you into three stores. I love the shoes! I don't want the tour.
Spencer just offered me a final two. That's... actually a good deal. Too bad I already have three other final deals. [pauses] Okay, four. Maybe five. The point is, I'm covered.
I’m not panicking. I’m paying attention. There’s a difference. Hannah usually tells me things, so when she doesn’t, I notice.

trivia: She approached Diego on the first day with a candy apple.
She broke off a small piece of her food and held it out in episode 9.
She reacted to winning with a shouted “WE WON!”

placements.name: Richard
placements.notes: Richard is the returning hero-provider whose integrity and loyalty make him valuable until Hannah's negotiated flip makes him the consensus sacrifice.
placements.story: Richard's first game ends on Blue Team as the honorable provider caught in shifting alliances, but Rescue Island hardens him rather than erases him. He returns at the merge stronger, more observant, and more socially grounded. His bonds with Marissa, Logan, and Ivy give him real protection, and his provider role makes him useful in a starving camp. But Richard's game is too honest for a board full of secret pivots. At final ten, Hannah identifies him as the vote that can unite competing rooms, and the move spreads faster than he can counter it. He leaves with his integrity intact, but his second chance ends as proof that decency is not always armor.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Searched for an idol clue and came up empty, immediately drawing attention.
Episode 7: Was voted out by Blue Team after being labeled a challenge liability.
Episode 13: Became one of Rescue Island's strongest return contenders through training and camp work.
Episode 16: Won his way back from the Edge alongside Ivy.
Episode 16: Learned Logan had broken their Final Two promise, ending that route.
Episode 17: Was targeted by Hannah's negotiated flip and eliminated in a 7-3 vote.
Episode 17: Left worrying about Marissa being unprotected.
placements.personality: Richard was loyal, physical and straightforward, with a strong sense that the game should reward work and commitment. He wanted an idol as a “weapon,” but he also talked about loyalty mattering even when it cost him. On Rescue Island, he became a survival-minded presence who kept working, organized when needed, and reminded himself to stay in uniform as long as there was time on the clock.

quotes.text: A pot? I got kids at home. I've got pots. I need a WEAPON in this game. An idol is a weapon. And if I find it — nobody has to know how I got the clue.
I'd do it again. I'd play the same game. Loyalty matters. Even if it costs me.
quotes.context: in confessional after being voted out

quotes.text: Getting voted out hurts. I’d be lying if I said it didn’t. But I’m still in uniform, and as long as there’s time on the clock, you keep playing.

trivia: He lost his idol clue and worried it might be in the shelter he helped Lynda “fix.”
He denied suspicious behavior by saying, “[to no one] I was whistling.”
He looped a rope around Tristan’s waist during a Rescue Island scene.

placements.name: Benji
placements.notes: Benji is an early puppetmaster and emotional connector who dodges vote after vote until a chaotic three-way tiebreaker ends him.
placements.story: Benji looks harmless at first, but by the second vote the game is already moving through him. He builds trust with Jade, Ivy, Hannah, and Spencer while keeping his own intentions soft enough to deny. His relationships become a web: Ivy, Hannah, Diego, and later The Movement all pull him in different directions. For a while, that web catches every fall, and he survives five tribals where his name keeps circling. But the same loyalty brand that protects him makes betrayal feel explosive when Marissa and Anastasia write him down. In the Haunted House vote, the board fractures beyond repair, and Benji loses the endurance tiebreaker to Zaid. The kingmaker is dethroned, stunned that loyalty did not come back to save him.
keyMoments: Episode 2: Helped The Anchor eliminate Amelie while being publicly accused as a smiling strategist.
Episode 4: Couldn't vote Jade and redirected onto Tristan, helping force Diego's tiebreaker loss.
Episode 9: Voted Zaid instead of Alessio, exposing fractures in The Ivy Core.
Episode 12: His bond with Ivy ended when Ivy was voted out, collapsing a major emotional pillar.
Episode 14: Played an Extra Vote for Natalia during the chaotic merge vote.
Episode 15: Was eliminated in a three-way tiebreaker against Spencer and Zaid.
Episode 15: Left furious at Anastasia and Marissa for betraying him.
placements.personality: Benji was eager, emotional and desperate to be trusted. He reacted to Jade sharing information with wide-eyed excitement, leaked things he should not have leaked, and carried guilt over writing the wrong name at Tribal. Even when others underestimated him, he noticed injuries, kept the fire going so Jade could sleep, fixed tents, and tried to turn loyalty into something useful.

quotes.text: Jade trusts ME with information? Me?! Okay, Benji. Play it cool. Play it — [he's already smiling too wide] — okay I'm not playing it cool. That's fine. That's fine.
quotes.context: in confessional after Jade tells him information

quotes.text: I lost Diego. I panicked at Tribal and wrote the wrong name and it cost me the best guy in this game. So when Zaid — ZAID — puts his hand out and says "final two"... [voice catching] Man. Yeah. I'm not messing this one up.
Hannah talks to me like I’m twelve. I’m not twelve. A twelve-year-old probably knows more about rationing, but that’s not the point.

trivia: He told Diego information after being told not to tell Diego, then got confused while explaining it.
He used all the dry firewood to cook one cup of rice.
He told a long cow joke with a completely serious punchline: “Because I don't feel like walking.”

placements.name: Natalia
placements.notes: Natalia is a chaos agent whose reads and aggression keep her relevant until her unpredictability becomes impossible to manage.
placements.story: Natalia arrives promising to learn the rules and break them, and she spends the season doing both. On Blue Team, she moves through alliances quickly: The Triumvirate, The Secret Weapon, Anti-Spencer arrangements, and temporary truces with people she distrusts. She is perceptive, confrontational, and repeatedly close to power without ever staying fully inside it. Her stage disaster in Talent Show hurts her image, but she keeps surviving through pressure, side deals, and social intimidation. At the merge, her threat level is too high to ignore and her enemies too numerous to outmaneuver. She leaves by exposing Logan and Anastasia's roles, turning her exit into one last detonation.
keyMoments: Episode 3: Helped form The Triumvirate, then immediately fractured it by voting Richard.
Episode 4: Was MVP of Paintball Hunt as the last deer standing.
Episode 6: Choked in Talent Show after Spencer sabotaged her props, scoring zero.
Episode 10: Faced Lynda in exile and stayed alive by winning the duel.
Episode 11: Survived while Lynda was sent permanently to Rescue Island.
Episode 14: Was voted out at the merge after being labeled unpredictable and a jury threat.
Episode 14: Exposed Logan and the Anti-Spencer Coalition in her crashout.
placements.personality: Natalia was guarded, observant and quick to remember who had underestimated or excluded her. She clocked Ted and Zaid early, watched Anastasia’s body language closely enough to infer a totem, and used false information as a test. Her frustration often came from feeling blamed while holding things together, but she rarely stopped tracking the board around her.

quotes.text: Zaid. Nice hair. Nice face. Watch him.
She has the Totem. She didn't say it. But she didn't NOT say it. And she thinks I found out by accident. I did not find out by accident. I've been watching her walk funny for two days.
Isabel thinks he’s hers. Marissa thinks he’s hers. Anastasia thinks he’s hers. Spencer built an alliance around him.

trivia: She locked eyes with Zaid for two full seconds on the first day, and neither of them smiled.
She noticed Isabel’s cold shoulder in small details, including Isabel saying “mm” like Natalia had coughed on her.
She was already awake when someone passed her bed in episode 11.

placements.name: Lynda
placements.notes: Lynda is a hotheaded advantage holder whose extra vote never becomes the weapon her personality suggests it might.
placements.story: Lynda finds the first advantage of the season and immediately becomes the kind of player everyone watches without fully trusting. She bounces between real bonds with Logan, Alessio, Isabel, and Marissa, and explosive hatred with Anastasia. Her alliances — The Firewall, The Secret Weapon, and The Ride or Die — never fully stabilize because Lynda keeps choosing emotion at the exact moments structure is required. She survives multiple brushes with danger, including an exile twist, but each escape costs trust. By Episode 11, her reputation as a flipper catches up, and Natalia beats her in the Exile Duel. Lynda leaves having made the waves she promised, even if they drowned her game.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Found the Extra Vote while collecting water and told nobody.
Episode 3: Formed The Firewall with Alessio.
Episode 6: Formed The Secret Weapon with Natalia against Anastasia.
Episode 7: Betrayed Alessio by voting him instead of Richard, cracking The Firewall.
Episode 10: Was sent to exile instead of being fully eliminated.
Episode 11: Lost the Exile Duel to Natalia and was sent to Rescue Island.
Episode 11: Left with a fiery speech about making waves.
placements.personality: Lynda was calm, efficient and quietly ruthless, preferring to set up failures that could be blamed on someone else later. She liked being underestimated as the “mom who tags along,” while privately managing extra votes, partnerships and rifts between other players. Her control frayed as alliances became exhausting and personal, especially when she recognized Isabel using her own methods against her.

quotes.text: [tilting head] The thing about a shelter is you don't need it to fall down. You need it to fail LATER. When someone else can be blamed. [pause] I'm not a bad person. I'm just an efficient one.

Marissa can yell at me by the horses all day. I'm not sorry. I have an extra vote in my sock and a partner in Alessio and a rift between her and Isabel that is doing more work than any log I could carry. So — [waves funnel cake] enjoy the moral high ground, sweetie.
quotes.context: in confessional after conflict with Marissa

quotes.text: People think I'm just the mom who tags along. That's fine. Let them think that. I know exactly what I'm doing.

trivia: She stopped in the middle of a path to crouch over a snail.
She hid an extra vote in her sock.
She ate something grey and stringy from a paper tray because she had dared herself to.

placements.name: Alessio
placements.notes: Alessio is a wildcard provider and quiet connector whose split alliances leave him exposed before the merge.
placements.story: Alessio starts as the person nobody can quite read, which makes him funny, useful, and dangerous in small doses. He finds real bonds with Logan, Lynda, Marissa, and Richard, then becomes part of The Firewall with Lynda. But when Lynda betrays that structure and the swap separates them, Alessio's protection erodes. On Red Team, he is never fully integrated into Jade's network, and Jade openly dislikes him. His challenge competence and camp work cannot overcome being the easiest name in a split field. He exits regretting that Marissa no longer has him watching her back, a quiet loyalty note in a season full of loud betrayals.
keyMoments: Episode 2: Beat Jade in the Bone Battle, giving Blue Team a crucial point.
Episode 3: Formed The Firewall with Lynda.
Episode 7: Was betrayed by Lynda when she voted for him instead of Richard.
Episode 8: Swapped onto Red Team after Spencer was voted out-but-swapped.
Episode 9: Overheard Jade pitching Benji on voting him out during Merry-Go-Round-Up.
Episode 9: Was eliminated by Jade and Zaid after the fractured Red Team vote.
Episode 13: Became a steadying presence on Rescue Island before falling short of the return.
placements.personality: Alessio was odd, gentle and distracted by details other people barely noticed. He worried about raccoons, snails, rust on carousel bolts and whether he was playing correctly, while also recognizing that Lynda was dangerous. His social reads were quiet and strange rather than forceful, and when conflict hit him he often retreated into short, careful answers.

quotes.text: I'm from a place where you don't just... crush stuff. To see. What's inside. I feed raccoons cotton candy. I do NOT autopsy the snails.
Lynda's terrifying. She's like a grandma with a knife hidden in her knitting. And she's on my tribe, which is either the best or the worst thing that's happened to me.
Perhaps she grew tired of the arrangement. Perhaps I did not notice because I was thinking about the way rust forms around the carousel bolts. That happens sometimes.
quotes.context: in confessional after Lynda betrays him

trivia: His first scene had him crouched away from the group, watching a raccoon eat cotton candy off the ground.
He described fog as “persuasive.”
He remained in his cage watching the timing during episode 16.

placements.name: Tristan
placements.notes: Tristan is an early underdog whose likeability keeps them close until the tribe decides closeness itself is the threat.
placements.story: Tristan opens the season with humor, warmth, and enough physical grit to surprise people. They beat Isabel in the Bone Battle and keep Red Team's mood alive through jokes, songs, and quiet deflections. But as Red Team fractures, Tristan becomes trapped between loyalty to Zaid's side and suspicion from everyone else. Their social value becomes a liability after Diego's elimination, especially once the tribe is desperate for a clean target. At Episode 5, Hannah and Ivy refuse to write Jade's name, and Tristan becomes the compromise nobody fully wants but enough people accept. On Rescue Island, they grow into one of the emotional backbones, saving Ted in the storm and proving the game cut them before their story was done.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Bonded with Zaid over host impressions and became an early camp mood-setter.
Episode 2: Beat Isabel in the Bone Battle with a clean low strike.
Episode 4: Survived a tied vote after Diego lost the puzzle tiebreaker.
Episode 5: Was targeted as a jury favorite and voted out by Jade, Spencer, Ivy, and Hannah.
Episode 13: Rescued Ted during the Rescue Island storm.
Episode 16: Fell in the Edge return gauntlet's first stage but left with grace.
placements.personality: Tristan was laid-back on the surface but constantly filing away information. They noticed Amelie overplaying, Spencer supervising instead of carrying lumber, and early pairs forming before the first day had even settled. After isolation and uncertainty, Tristan’s confessionals became less snarky and more direct about wanting people to notice them and making any “almost” vote matter.

quotes.text: Amelie's pulling people aside. Spencer and Hannah are making eyes over a pot. And now Jade and Zaid are having a secret walk. Day one, guys. Day ONE. I haven't even brushed my teeth.
She's spiraling. I said it night one — four people in one night. Now it's like nine people in one afternoon. You can't hug your way to the merge. I've tried.
Last night, you weren’t the guy I have to beat.

trivia: Anastasia’s silent stare made Tristan freeze mid-laugh on the first day.
Tristan sat alone by the fire with arms around their knees after a challenge before Benji approached.
They brought Richard water on Rescue Island.

placements.name: Diego
placements.notes: Diego plays a clean, loyal early game that ends by the thinnest possible margin in a tiebreaker.
placements.story: Diego enters looking for the experience, and for four episodes he plays with sincerity that stands out in a cast full of schemers. His bonds with Benji and Hannah, and his quiet loyalty to Jade, make him deeply trusted but strategically passive. Physically, he gives Red Team real strength, hauling shelter parts and winning his Bone Battle against Logan. But when Red Team fractures, Diego cannot bring himself to write Jade's name, and that mercy costs him. A 3-3 tie sends him into a puzzle tiebreaker against Tristan, and he loses. His exit is clean, painful, and remembered as one of the season's narrowest cuts.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Hauled a Ferris-wheel cart during Shelter Scramble and gave Red Team a head start.
Episode 2: Beat Logan in the Bone Battle with a decisive smash.
Episode 3: Quietly redirected a plan against Benji without asking for credit.
Episode 4: Refused to vote Jade and wrote Tristan instead.
Episode 4: Lost the challenge tiebreaker to Tristan and was eliminated.
Episode 4: Learned at Aftermath that Jade had voted him out, deepening the sting.
placements.personality: Diego was physical, proud and trying to prove he belonged without playing dirty. He admitted early that he did not have an alliance or another plan, but he still wanted people to know he had done something. His clean-game instinct mattered to him: even when Jade was an available target, he remembered that she had treated him like a human and refused to write her name.

quotes.text: Zaid said Spencer. Okay. I don't have another plan. I don't have an alliance. I nod. I need them to know I was here. That I did something. Anything.
quotes.context: in confessional about an early vote

quotes.text: [grinning, out of breath] This is what I love about this game. You give me a paintball gun in the woods? I'm dangerous.
Three guys shook my hand and wrote my name. And I still don't regret not writing Jade's. That's the game I want to play. I'm not done.
quotes.context: in confessional after his torch is snuffed

trivia: He walked a cart across the lot like it was a duffel bag on the first day.
When his trapdoor opened, he calmly stepped down before it fully opened, refusing the drama.
He said the shelter post split on Rescue Island and offered to restart the fire because he knew how.

placements.name: Ted
placements.notes: Ted is an early schemer whose honest core and late read leave him one vote behind the game.
placements.story: Ted arrives thinking three steps ahead, but Blue Team's chaos moves faster than his calculations. He builds small bonds with Logan and Richard, tries to plant context around Marissa and Richard, and keeps presenting himself as steady. The problem is that everyone reads him as flexible before he can prove he is loyal. At the Truth or Dare Train tribal, he sees the shape of the vote too late, and the consensus lands before he can counter. His exit speech nails Anastasia as a driver, giving the jury its first public strategic breadcrumb. On Rescue Island and at the motel, Ted becomes more reflective than bitter, a player who understands the game best after it has already passed him.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Worked with Isabel to shift her read on Marissa through careful 'context'.
Episode 3: Completed the eyebrow-shaving dare without flinching.
Episode 3: Tried to vote Richard while the majority landed on him.
Episode 3: Was eliminated 5-3 after identifying the counter window too late.
Episode 3: Exposed Anastasia's role in his last words.
Episode 13: Was rescued by Tristan during the Rescue Island storm.
placements.personality: Ted was chatty, self-justifying and increasingly urgent once he realized he was in danger. He distinguished “framing” from lying, tried to redirect names, and openly called out the tribe when they voted the way Anastasia wanted. On Rescue Island, his focus turned toward earning a second chance, though he still showed awkward warmth by approaching people with food and admitting when he barely knew them.

quotes.text: I didn't lie to Isabel. I didn't. I just... framed something. That's not lying, that's — that's cooking. You take a raw thing and you cook it. [nods to himself] Yeah.
Richard just told me I'm on the block. And he's right. I can feel it. I've been quiet all day and it hasn't helped. So tonight I stop being quiet.
I called it. I called it and you still did it. That's on you.

trivia: Natalia clocked him immediately as a nice, chatty person with a thought on everyone.
He covered his face during a Rescue Island scene.
He later approached carrying two plates of fries.

placements.name: Amelie
placements.notes: Amelie overplays first, exposes alliances on the way out, and becomes the season's original warning about moving too fast.
placements.story: Amelie comes in calling the game a chess match, then burns through her opening moves before anyone else has finished setting the board. She has useful instincts — physical competence, social reads, and a willingness to name threats — but she pulls too many people too quickly. Her jealousy of Jade and discomfort with The Anchor's consolidation make her an easy first boot once Red Team loses. At tribal, she stays composed until the votes fall, then uses her exit to detonate Benji's role and expose The Zaid Four. On Rescue Island, she trains hard, heals, and remains sharp-tongued to the end. Her game is short, but it defines the season's first rule: personality is not protection.
keyMoments: Episode 1: Helped steady Benji during Shelter Scramble after the pigeon scare.
Episode 2: Overplayed by pulling too many people aside before the first Red Team vote.
Episode 2: Left a forged note that shook Jade's read on Hannah.
Episode 2: Broke from The Zaid Four's plan and voted Ivy.
Episode 2: Was voted out 5-1-1-2 and sent to Rescue Island.
Episode 4: Took an Aftermath anvil when her Ivy vote was exposed.
Episode 16: Fell in the Edge return gauntlet's social stage with a cold exit.
placements.personality: Amelie began as aggressively friendly, pulling people aside and trying to make “same page” connections until others felt smothered. After being voted out, she reframed herself as tougher and more focused, practicing puzzles and insisting “Sweet Amelie stays on the beach.” She could still be blunt and sarcastic, especially around Rescue Island planning and Ivy’s influence.

quotes.text: They think I'm out here crying about it. I'm not crying about it. I'm doing this puzzle in forty-two seconds. Yesterday it was fifty-one. When they open that gate for a duel, I'm walking through it. Sweet Amelie stays on the beach.
Ivy voted me out. My best friend on Red. I'm going back in there, and when I do — she's gonna wish she'd taken the anvil.
Stop saying that like all lies are the same.

trivia: She arranged pine needles inside the first Red shelter like a nesting bird.
Her face went perfectly frozen when the vote turned against her.
She practiced a puzzle down from fifty-one seconds to forty-two seconds on Rescue Island.

finalTribalCouncil.note: No jury — winner decided by the final challenge.

seasonNarrative: Carnival of Chaos is a season where the midway never stops taking payment. The pre-merge is built on unstable shelters, food scarcity, Rescue Island pressure, and alliances that form quickly because nobody feels safe for long. Jade and Spencer begin as mutual respect and end as open hatred; Anastasia and Isabel turn Blue Team into a war zone; Benji, Ivy, Zaid, Hannah, and Marissa prove that showmances and ride-or-die bonds can be both shelter and target. The merge detonates the game: idols wipe votes, extra votes fail to control chaos, the Edge returns Ivy and Richard, and the jury starts tracking who it believes is really running each boot. By the endgame, shields become threats one by one — Richard, Ivy, Zaid, Marissa, Isabel, Spencer, Hannah, and Anastasia all fall as their stories become too visible. The finale strips away the jury vote and asks only who can finish the Carnival Rescue. Jade answers with the same thing that carried her all season: read the pattern, cut through the noise, and do not look back.

bestStrategic.name: Anastasia
bestStrategic.description: Anastasia had the highest strategic résumé: idol timing, vote influence, late-game immunity wins, and repeated jury credit for control, even though that visibility ultimately got her cut.

bestSocial.name: Ted
bestSocial.description: Ted's average bonds were the strongest on paper, and his post-game arc showed a player whose honesty and calm made people open up even after his early exit.

bestPhysical.name: Jade
bestPhysical.description: Jade tied the season high in challenge wins and took the final challenge when it mattered most, turning physical and mental composure into the title.

mostClutch.name: Jade
mostClutch.description: From the Zaid idol save to late immunities to the final Carnival Rescue, Jade repeatedly landed the exact move or win she needed at the edge of disaster.

mostLoyal.name: Diego
mostLoyal.description: Diego refused to write Jade's name even when it was strategically safer, and his clean loyalty became both his identity and his downfall.

bestUnderdog.name: Tristan
bestUnderdog.description: Tristan survived a tiebreaker scare, fought from the bottom, and then became one of Rescue Island's emotional anchors despite leaving early.

biggestVillain.name: Isabel
biggestVillain.description: Isabel weaponized confidence, intimidation, lies, and idol timing while feuding with half the cast, earning the season's clearest villain edit.

mostChaotic.name: Jade
mostChaotic.description: Jade's game produced idol saves, personal betrayals, challenge sabotage, public blowups, and finale dominance — chaos with a compass.

quietestThreat.name: Logan
quietestThreat.description: Logan hid behind warmth and usefulness while becoming a vote broker, challenge threat, and endgame shield nobody could fully remove.

seasonMVP.name: Jade
seasonMVP.description: Jade was the season's central force: winner, challenge closer, feud magnet, idol player, and repeated endgame decision-maker.

mostTragic.name: Hannah
mostTragic.description: Hannah built real bonds everywhere, only to be cut at final four by people she thought had crossed from strategy into something genuine.

mostUnlucky.name: Diego
mostUnlucky.description: Diego's game ended not by majority collapse but by a tied vote and puzzle tiebreaker, the narrowest and cruelest kind of early exit.

ironPerson.name: Spencer
ironPerson.description: Spencer absorbed 19 votes across the season, survived eight dangerous tribals, and kept fighting until final five.

biggestMeltdown.name: Benji
biggestMeltdown.description: Benji's Episode 15 unraveling after the Ivy-Hannah-Zaid emotional triangle and alliance pressure exposed the cracks in his carefully gentle game.

gold.name: Jade
gold.description: Jade wins the season and defines its strategic endgame, earning the top player spot through survival, control, and final execution.

silver.name: Anastasia
silver.description: Anastasia had the strongest non-winning résumé and would have been a nightmare finalist if the jury had not removed her at third.

gold.name: Marissa
gold.description: Marissa's rescue of Zaid underwater, loyalty to her people, and repeated provider role made her the season's clearest hero.

silver.name: Richard
silver.description: Richard played with integrity, protected others, and returned from the Edge as a provider before being sacrificed by a numbers move.

gold.name: Isabel
gold.description: Isabel's arrogance, idol play, feuds, and cutting social style made her the season's signature villain.

silver.name: Anastasia
silver.description: Anastasia's controlling reputation, idol theatrics, and brutal betrayals gave her a darker strategic edge.

gold.name: Jade
gold.description: Jade won three challenges including the final, and repeatedly converted safety into control.

silver.name: Anastasia
silver.description: Anastasia also won three immunities and survived multiple rounds purely because rivals could not touch her.

gold.name: Hannah
gold.description: Hannah's social reach shaped votes, repaired moods, and made her too dangerous to sit beside at the end.

silver.name: Marissa
silver.description: Marissa built deep loyalty with Logan, Anastasia, Zaid, Hannah, and Richard, making her a major jury threat.

gold.name: Anastasia
gold.description: Anastasia received repeated jury credit for running votes and used advantages, immunity, and fear to stay alive.

silver.name: Jade
silver.description: Jade's quieter endgame architecture delivered the actual win and multiple credited boots.

gold.name: Anastasia
gold.description: Anastasia survived to final three only to be removed by the jury after Logan's immunity, a brutal reversal for a player built for Final Tribal.

silver.name: Spencer
silver.description: After dodging eight tribals, Spencer was finally undone by visible overplaying and cut just short of the final four.

gold.name: Anastasia
gold.description: Anastasia found an idol, played it to erase four votes, bought a Vote Steal, and used that advantage to shape the Ivy boot.

silver.name: Jade
silver.description: Jade found an idol and used protection dramatically, most notably saving Zaid while deepening her loyalist image.

gold.name: Anastasia
gold.description: Anastasia had the season's best strategic score and three immunities, but the jury twist removed her before she could argue her case.

gold.name: Jade
gold.description: With no jury vote, Jade's FTC-equivalent was the final challenge itself, and she delivered the only argument that mattered: victory.

gold.name: Logan
gold.description: Logan reached the final with a strong social-physical résumé, but the final format denied him a jury case and forced everything onto one race.

messiestFeud.description: Their feud lasted from Blue Team through the endgame: intimidation, accusations, idol paranoia, crossed votes, and a final Isabel boot fueled by pure hostility.

biggestBetrayal.description: Jade joined the brand-new Power Couple structure, then flipped onto Spencer after his overplaying, ending a season-long rivalry disguised briefly as cooperation.

secondBiggestBetrayal.description: Anastasia told the Power Couple one thing and secretly put the decisive votes on Hannah, cutting a daily confidante at final four.

legacyMoment.name: Marissa rescues Zaid underwater
legacyMoment.description: In the Treasure Island challenge, Marissa abandoned a possible win to save Zaid from drowning, creating the season's defining hero moment and altering the emotional map of the merge.

fanFavorite.name: Zaid
fanFavorite.description: Zaid was the season's most popular player with the fans.

gameHistory.title: Amelie Spiraled
gameHistory.prose: Red struggled after the challenge, and Amelie’s intense attempts to connect with everyone made several tribemates uncomfortable. Jade spent the day testing Benji with false information and confirmed that he leaked it, while Zaid hesitated and voted alone rather than joining the main plan. Ivy was reluctant but ultimately wrote Amelie’s name after feeling crowded by her behavior. Amelie was eliminated and sent to Rescue Island, while Red returned to camp aware that Zaid had isolated himself with his vote.

gameHistory.title: Ted Spoke Up
gameHistory.prose: On Blue, Lynda quietly deepened the rift between Isabel and Marissa by planting a note that made Isabel believe Marissa had insulted her. Ted sensed he was in danger and tried to stop being passive, but Anastasia’s push against him held together despite his warning. Logan wanted to stay loyal to Richard and assumed the numbers would work, while Natalia treated Richard as expendable if needed. Ted was eliminated and went to Rescue Island, where he made it clear he blamed Anastasia for directing the vote.

gameHistory.title: Anastasia Found Safety
gameHistory.prose: Anastasia staged a public conflict with Richard to get away from Blue camp and search, successfully finding a hidden totem. On Red, Jade continued testing Benji, while Diego, Benji, Tristan, and Zaid discussed targeting Jade before Diego backed away from writing her name. Zaid pushed Tristan as the better long-term target, but the vote did not land there. Diego was eliminated and arrived on Rescue Island with Amelie and Ted.

gameHistory.title: Spencer's Note
gameHistory.prose: Jade stayed quiet after surviving the previous vote, which made Spencer increasingly anxious and caused him to lash out at Hannah. Zaid offered Benji a final two after Diego’s exit, but Spencer planted a note to make Benji question Zaid’s loyalty. Ivy redirected the anti-Jade vote onto Tristan while keeping Benji out of the true plan, leaving him to think he was following the safer option. Tristan was eliminated and joined the others on Rescue Island.

gameHistory.title: Firewall Broken
gameHistory.prose: Red built more overlapping deals, with Hannah and Ivy growing closer and Spencer offering Ivy a final two while Benji tried to secure himself with Jade. On Blue, Anastasia tried to repair damage from earlier comments, but Natalia tested her with false information and Lynda remained wary. After Blue lost the challenge, Marissa and Logan appeared aligned on the vote, while Lynda’s choice to turn on her own ally unsettled Natalia. Richard was eliminated and sent to Rescue Island, leaving Lynda isolated and the Blue tribe unsure what her move meant.

gameHistory.title: The Team Swap
gameHistory.prose: Lynda’s vote against Richard left Alessio feeling betrayed, though she framed it as an ugly move rather than a bad one. Red’s loss put pressure on Ivy, Spencer, and Benji, with Jade and Ivy both weighing Spencer’s value against the danger he posed. At the elimination, Red voted, but the round ended with no contestant eliminated. Instead, Spencer was moved to Blue and Alessio was sent to Red, giving Spencer access to the other half of the game.

gameHistory.title: Jade Played Idol
gameHistory.prose: After the swap, Alessio tried to fit into Red by working carefully around camp, but he quickly stood out as an outsider. Zaid secretly had an idol and handed it to Jade before elimination, while Red’s relationships around Benji, Hannah, Ivy, and Jade continued to strain. Jade played the idol at the vote, changing the outcome. Alessio was eliminated and sent to Rescue Island.

gameHistory.title: Lynda Sent Away
gameHistory.prose: Red dealt with the fallout of Jade’s idol play, as Benji and Zaid remained tense and Jade worked to regain trust. On Blue, Natalia, Isabel, Lynda, Anastasia, Logan, Marissa, and Spencer maneuvered around fractured loyalties, with Natalia feeding information and Anastasia keeping her idol unused. The vote produced a tie and then a revote, after which Lynda was sent to Exile rather than leaving the game outright. Blue returned to camp split into separate groups, while Lynda was left alone in the sideshow tent.

gameHistory.title: Exile Duel
gameHistory.prose: Blue entered the round divided after the previous revote, with Natalia noting that Isabel and Logan had both shifted onto Lynda. Lynda trained alone on Exile while Blue lost again and prepared for another vote, with Spencer encouraging Natalia and making her believe he was voting Isabel. Anastasia considered her hidden idol but did not play it, exposing how much attention the tribe was paying to her bag. Natalia was sent into a duel against Lynda and won, causing Lynda to be eliminated and sent to Rescue Island.

gameHistory.title: Benji Saved Zaid
gameHistory.prose: The merge was announced, but the former Red and Blue groups still lived with their old divisions during the challenge. Red lost after the elephant challenge, despite Benji pulling Zaid out of danger and helping secure the final ladder piece. Back at camp, Jade and Zaid stayed close, while Ivy tried to hold her position between Benji, Hannah, and the others. Ivy was eliminated and chose the Rescue Island path.

gameHistory.title: Extra Vote Exposed
gameHistory.prose: At the merged camp, Benji found an Extra Vote at the water pump and hid it from Zaid, worsening the tension between them. During the underwater challenge, Marissa rescued Zaid after he became trapped, while Logan and Isabel won immunity by securing the chest. Before the vote, Anastasia held her bag close and Benji kept touching the Extra Vote, signaling that advantages might decide the round. Anastasia played her Hidden Immunity Idol, Benji used the Extra Vote, and Natalia was eliminated, leaving for Rescue Island without stopping.

gameHistory.title: Haunted Mansion Tie
gameHistory.prose: Anastasia and Marissa’s bond grew after Natalia’s exit, while Benji remained shaken and isolated from the fight around Logan, Zaid, and the larger group. Anastasia won immunity in the haunted mansion challenge after outlasting Spencer in the final duel. Around camp, Marissa, Logan, Zaid, and Anastasia coordinated, while a note was planted to influence Hannah and the vote fractured badly. Spencer, Zaid, and Benji were forced into a tiebreaker, and Benji was eliminated after falling first.

gameHistory.title: Richard Returned Briefly
gameHistory.prose: Richard returned to the game but found camp dynamics had already moved on, with Logan’s things occupying his old space and Jade watching him closely. Marissa won immunity in the shark-tank challenge, and afterward several groups formed competing plans around Richard, Hannah, and Logan’s numbers. Logan pushed Richard’s name even though he had worked with him before, while Marissa and Ivy exchanged a look that showed the vote was not simple for them. Richard was eliminated again, leaving Marissa frozen and Logan sitting alone after the vote.

gameHistory.title: Auction Vote Steal
gameHistory.prose: The auction gave Anastasia a Vote Steal with Marissa’s help, Spencer immunity, Isabel an idol clue, and Zaid an emotional message from home that visibly affected Ivy and Hannah. Ivy tried to build a move with Jade, Hannah, Zaid, and Marissa, but Jade rejected it and Ivy’s fight with Hannah damaged her position. Logan, Jade, Isabel, Marissa, and Anastasia countered while Zaid was caught between Ivy and the rest of the group. Anastasia used the Vote Steal to cast an extra ballot against Ivy, and Ivy was eliminated after an emotional crashout.

gameHistory.title: Killer Clown Hunt
gameHistory.prose: Zaid struggled after Ivy’s elimination, while Jade pushed hidden food into the open and Spencer rapidly worked the remaining players. In the killer clown challenge, Anastasia secured immunity first, while Zaid was repeatedly attacked and finished last despite keeping his flag. Back at camp, Jade campaigned against Zaid, the Ride or Die group met, and Logan and Isabel considered whether to protect or cut him. An idol was played at Tribal Council, and Zaid was eliminated after another emotional outburst.

gameHistory.title: Marissa's Goodbye
gameHistory.prose: Anastasia realized her Vote Steal was gone and leaned on Marissa as the two continued working together around camp. Anastasia won immunity in the hedge maze, while Marissa was sent to the pit after answering wrong and later tried to campaign against Isabel. Spencer and Isabel pushed the vote toward Marissa, and Logan did not save her despite her close ties to him and Anastasia. Marissa was eliminated, leaving Anastasia devastated and returning to camp with Marissa’s blanket and the carnival cat beside her.

gameHistory.title: Five Separate Spaces
gameHistory.prose: After Marissa left, Anastasia withdrew under Marissa’s blanket but briefly reconnected with Logan during the mud punishment. Jade and Logan won immunity together in the Ferris wheel challenge, while Isabel continued trying to position herself with Spencer and Logan. Jade overheard Hannah and Spencer talking and moved with Hannah before Tribal, while Anastasia and Isabel openly clashed. Isabel was eliminated, and the remaining five returned to camp separated into different spaces.

gameHistory.title: Fairy Tale Betrayal
gameHistory.prose: The final five received letters and briefly softened toward each other before the game resumed. Anastasia won immunity in the fairy-tale challenge after defeating Spencer in the tower duel, while Logan later tried to steer Jade toward voting Hannah. Hannah tested Logan with the forged note and then defended Jade when Spencer, Logan, and Anastasia discussed options near the shelter. At Tribal Council, Spencer kept whispering conflicting plans, Jade flipped, and Spencer was eliminated.

gameHistory.title: Bumper Car Immunity
gameHistory.prose: After Spencer’s exit, Hannah realized she had been left out of the final decision and the distance between her and Jade became visible in the shelter. Logan and Hannah worked well together around camp, while Jade watched them and Anastasia noticed Jade’s reaction. Jade won immunity in the bumper-car challenge after Logan blocked her from losing the final exchange with Anastasia. Jade voted for Anastasia, but the vote sent Hannah out instead, and Hannah was eliminated after a quiet goodbye to the arena and the remaining players.
